tools.name: search_sounds
tools.description: Free-text search over the SFXMint library of free CC0 sound effects. Use it for sound descriptions, additional constraints or gaps left by another tool. Choose get_role_sound for a named event or get_sound_set for multiple events when that fits the task; these are task branches, not a fixed sequence

tools.name: get_role_sound
tools.description: Choose this when the task calls for a sound for a named event or interaction — a button click, purchase success, error beep, level-up, dialogue blip, notification. Pass the role as plain words: role ids (click, success, purchase-success, dialogue-blip, notification…) and common aliases (button click

tools.name: get_sound
tools.description: Get full metadata for one sound by slug, including download URLs, description and measured acoustics (attack/tail/brightness + character labels).

tools.name: get_sound_set
tools.description: Get a coherent set of sounds for an app or game in one call — one sound per role, with format metadata, hashes and stable download URLs. Use it when the task needs a whole kit; use get_role_sound for one event. Check content_check: verified/unverified/rejected is bound to the exact role, format and

tools.name: generate_sound
tools.description: Make a new sound effect from a description when the library has nothing suitable (search_sounds has no full match and its closest sounds do not suit; it then returns generate_available). Needs an SFXMint API key and a pass or plan on the account — a 24-hour pass ($3.90, 50 sounds) or a plan (from $9

tools.name: get_generation
tools.description: Check a generation started with generate_sound: status, and fresh download links for the finished takes.

tools.name: start_game_kit
tools.description: Start a Game kit: SFXMint plans the sounds one game needs and makes them as CC0 takes to pick from — the same project the user sees on the website. Use it when the user wants sounds for a whole game or scene and the library (get_sound_set, get_role_sound) does not cover them. Needs an SFXMint API ke

tools.name: add_kit_sounds
tools.description: Add the user's own list of sounds to a kit (an app's or a game's events: names, optional moments and lengths), or a ready set's events with its library sounds already in use. Names, keys, order and lengths stay the user's; SFXMint writes how each sounds. Without kit_id it starts a new kit for the li

tools.name: fill_kit_from_library
tools.description: Fill a kit's sounds from the free CC0 library first: each sound without a take is searched by its name and length, and a full match becomes its take in use, free. Answers what matched (let the user listen), the nearest sounds for others (use_library_sound to use one) and the gaps to make with make_k

tools.name: find_kit_sound_candidates
tools.description: Up to five free library sounds for one kit sound, by its name or your own words, with their length, character and a listening URL. Nothing changes until use_library_sound.

tools.name: use_library_sound
tools.description: Use a library sound (its slug) as a take of a kit sound, free. It becomes the take in use when the sound has none; otherwise it waits beside the others for the user to compare.

tools.name: get_game_kit
tools.description: A Game kit's state: its scenes, its sounds (event key, when it plays, status, the takes made with short-lived file links, SHA-256 and length, and the take in use), how its makes are paid (the account's plan's generations of the day, or the plan it needs) and next_step. Needs the API key that started

tools.name: list_kit_sounds
tools.description: List the sounds of a Game kit's scenes, free: after start_game_kit planned the scenes, show them to the user, then call this with the scenes to keep (all by default; the others are switched off). Call get_game_kit after about 15 seconds.

tools.name: make_kit_sounds
tools.description: Make sounds in a Game kit: each sound gets up to four takes, and each sound made is one generation. Each uses one of the account's plan generations of the day, shared with generate_sound; nothing is charged. Without a plan it answers payment_required with buy_url, and when the day's are used with pl

tools.name: pick_kit_take
tools.description: Use one of a sound's takes in the kit (the first take is used until the user picks). Let the user listen to the takes first.

tools.name: export_game_kit
tools.description: What to put in the project: every included sound's event key and the take in use (file link valid 15 minutes, SHA-256), the sounds not ready yet, and zip_url for one ZIP (download it with the same Authorization header) holding the files in the chosen format, sounds.json (event key → file) and a READ

findings.title: Description references secrets/credentials
findings.detail: Description of "export_game_kit" references sensitive artifacts (authorization). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.
